title: DC-SQEM: Medial Mesh Extraction by Dual Contouring with Spherical Quadric Error Metric
abstract: The medial axis , as a compact representation, describes not only the boundary but also the interior of the shape, and has been widely used in analyzing and simplifying shapes. However, approximating feature-preserving medial axis from unstructured data, such as oriented point clouds, remains challenging due to the lack of explicit connectivity and the presence of noise in the source. We propose DC-SQEM, a dual-contouring-based framework that computes medial meshes (an explicit representation of the medial axis) directly from oriented point clouds without relying on watertight manifold surfaces or volumetric structures. With the help of an adaptive octree, our method fits local medial spheres for each cell based on the Spherical Quadric Error Metric (SQEM). We address several long-standing robustness issues in dual-contouring and mesh extraction, including out-of-cell solutions, unstable feature classification, and redundant topological connections. To this end, we introduce virtual nodes, a feature-downgrading strategy, and a geometry-driven topology-aware cleanup procedure, enabling robust SQEM-based medial dual contouring with clean mesh outputs. Unlike prior point-cloud-based methods that produce either only 1D skeletal structures or incomplete medial features, our method preserves sharp geometric features from the input and reconstructs a complete medial structure, including sheets, curves, seams, and junctions. Compared to restricted-power-diagram-based approaches, our algorithm can handle point clouds as input, without having a strong requirement on water-tightness or manifoldness.

title: Regional-scale field-level estimation and mapping of tillage practices in areas with crop diversity
abstract: The imperative for sustainable agriculture has led to the promotion of conservation tillage practices, which are critical for maintaining soil health and reducing negative environmental impacts. However, the ability to verify the adoption of these practices at a regional scale and with minimal costs remains a challenge, particularly in regions with diverse crop systems. This study presents a satellite-imagery-based random forest classifier that integrates crop class information and a customized importance weighting technique for field-level, regional-scale mapping of tillage practices in crop-diverse regions. We use eastern Washington State, U.S., with multiple grains, legumes, and canola as a case study. Using 577 field-level ground-truth data points across two counties, the tillage classifier achieved a median overall accuracy of 84%, representing a 15 percentage point improvement over the baseline median overall accuracy of 69%, driven by the inclusion of crop class and the application of importance weighting. Specific crop classes, including grains, legumes, and canola, showed accuracy improvements of 6, 42, and 13 percentage points, respectively. While the model showed promising results, limitations such as overprediction of no-tillage in non-grain crop classes were identified, pointing to the need for further refinement with additional data. The model was applied to map tillage practices across dryland fields in eastern Washington State for the years 2012, 2017, and 2022, and the predictions were generally congruent with the USDA Census of Agriculture county-level statistics. This research offers a scalable tool for the verification of conservation tillage practice adoption, supporting both regional and global monitoring efforts for sustainable agricultural practices.
